question: Plants with green and tender stems are called __________.
solution:
The correct answer is__** Herbs**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plants** with green and tender stems are called herbs.
 
• **Herbs** are usually short, non-woody plants.
 
• They might be **annuals, biennials, or perennials, but the common feature is their soft, green, and tender stem structure.**
 
• Examples of herbs include **grasses, ferns, and certain types of flowering plants.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shrubs**:

 
 
• Shrubs are medium-sized, semi-woody plants.
 
• They are usually multi-stemmed, smaller than trees, and have a bushy appearance.
 
• Shrubs can be both evergreen or deciduous. Examples of shrubs include holly, rose, and azalea.
 
 
 
• **Trees: **
 
 
• Trees are tall, woody plants.
 
• They typically have a single main stem or trunk that grows to a considerable height and bear lateral branches.
 
• Examples include oaks, maples, and pines. They play a crucial role in producing oxygen and sequestering carbon dioxide.
 
 
 
• **Canopy: **
 
 
• Canopy refers to the overhead layer or habitat formed by mature tree crowns in a forest.
 
• It's not a type of plant, but rather a term that describes a particular layer within a forest ecosystem.
 
• The canopy provides shelter and habitat to various animals and plants.
 
 
 
• **Herbs: **
 
 
• Herbs are small, non-woody plants.
 
• They have green and tender stems.
 
• They usually die back to the ground at the end of each growing season.
 
• They can be annuals (life cycle completed in one growing season), biennials (life cycle completed in two growing seasons), or perennials (live for several to many growing seasons).
 
• Examples of herbs include basil, mint, and dill.
